_comment: Everything that depends on which GPU vendor a machine has, in one place,
keyed by SURFACING_GPU_BACKEND. Three consumers read it:
adapters/common.py   `env` — defines exported into every method
subprocess, before any torch code runs.
adapters/common.py   `methods.<name>` — per-method overrides for the
cases where a method is not one codebase but two.
`trellis` is the only one so far: upstream TRELLIS
is CUDA-only (custom kernels, xformers, flash-attn),
so AMD needs the TRELLIS-AMD fork — a different
checkout, a different venv, and HIP-only defines
(torchsparse instead of spconv, sdpa instead of
xformers). Same adapter, same parameters, same
results to compare; only the process differs.
cluster/setup_venvs.sh
`torch_index` — the download.pytorch.org index the
torch wheels come from, per venv, falling back to
`default`. torch is installed FIRST and never
appears in a requirements file, so this is the only
thing deciding whether a venv ends up ROCm or CUDA.
Before this file those two answers lived apart: the runtime read
SURFACING_GPU_BACKEND while the install read TORCH_INDEX/TORCH_INDEX_VNS,
typed on the command line and defaulting to ROCm. Setting the backend but
forgetting the indices installed ROCm torch on an NVIDIA machine, and
nothing failed until the first cell ran.
`repo` and `python` under a method are resolved relative to the server
directory, and ~ expands, so a checkout outside the project can be named
without hardcoding a home directory. Both are overridable per method by
env var (TRELLIS_REPO / TRELLIS_PYTHON) for a machine that keeps them
somewhere else again.
Device selection is deliberately NOT here. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES are set per worker by local/run_sweep.py (and by Slurm
on the cluster); a fixed value in this table would be a stale default that
every caller has to override.
An unknown backend is an error in every consumer rather than a fallback:
a typo silently running the wrong stack is the thing this file exists to
prevent.

_fill_holes: false because the fork's simplified coarse rasterizer returns
empty visibility, so TRELLIS's fill_holes marks every face
invisible and deletes the mesh (AMD_GPU_GUIDE.md 3.3). Not a
configuration problem: nvdiffrast-hip builds and runs, the stage
itself is wrong on AMD. The adapter clears loose fragments by
component area instead, which is cruder — it cannot tell a small
part from a stray shell, only small from large.
